_note: Online assessments. Data, not code: adding one means adding an entry here and its problems to problems/ with "pool": "assessment". Nothing in js/ needs editing. See README ▸ Online Assessments for the field-by-field meaning and scripts/check-assessments.mjs for what is validated.

_schema.id: stable, kebab-case, never reused — attempts are stored against it
_schema.version: integer. Bump when the problems, the scoring or the duration change. An attempt records the version it was taken under, so an old attempt is never re-scored against new rules.
_schema.title: what it is called
_schema.problems: ordered problem ids, all of them pool=assessment
_schema.langs: optional map of problem id to the languages permitted for it in this assessment. A subset of what the problem itself offers. Absent means all of them.

scoring.policy: weighted — each problem's score is its grader's 0..1 fraction times its weight
scoring.weights: map of problem id to weight. Absent entries weigh 1.
scoring.partialCredit: whether a problem's fractional score counts, or only a full pass does
scoring.passMark: fraction of the total needed to pass, or null for no pass/fail

feedback.duringAttempt: what you are told while it is running: 'samples' runs the visible cases only and reports them; 'none' reports nothing until you finish
feedback.hints: whether hints are available during the attempt
feedback.solutions: whether solutions can be revealed during the attempt

assessments.title: C++ foundations, timed
assessments.description: Three questions in forty-five minutes: what the compiler does to your types before it compares them, which of four functions hands back a reference to something already destroyed, and one program to write and get right. The problems are not in the practice catalogue, so you have not seen them.
